summary: Breuil, Herzig, Hu, Morra and Schraen prove that for a totally real F unramified at p > 2, an inert place v of degree f and a generic modular r: G_F → GL_2(F), the r-part of the mod p cohomology of Shimura curves at infinite level at v has Gelfand–Kirillov dimension f (Theorem 1.1). The proof combines a local criterion for GK dimension through the graded Iwasawa algebra of the pro-p Iwahori and multiplicity-one results (§§5–6), explicit lattices in projective envelopes (§7), and freeness of patched modules from explicit tame potentially Barsotti–Tate deformation rings (§§3–4, 8). Consequences include Banach lifts and flatness of completed cohomology over the big Hecke algebra. Complete (cc-442dc5, continuing cc-d67081): every numbered statement is an item and every missing item is routed exactly once; one misprint is recorded (E1). The proofs of §§4–8 were read at statement level and skimmed, not audited line by line, and no library declaration was matched. Not formalised.

items.name: Gelfand–Kirillov dimension of an admissible smooth representation
items.statement: For an admissible smooth representation π of GL2(Fv) over F, dim_{GL2(Fv)}(π) is the Gelfand–Kirillov dimension of its dual π^∨ as a finitely generated module over the Iwasawa algebra of a uniform open pro-p subgroup, following the review of Gelfand–Kirillov dimension in §5.1.
items.note: Statement from the paper's own formulation; hypotheses abbreviated as in §1.2 and §8.1.

items.name: Graded Iwasawa algebra of the pro-p Iwahori
items.statement: The graded ring gr_m F[[I1/Z1]] for the m-adic filtration is computed explicitly (Theorem 5.3.4); it is not commutative, since I1/Z1 is not uniform.
items.note: Statement from the paper's own formulation; hypotheses abbreviated as in §1.2 and §8.1.

items.name: Upper bound for the Gelfand–Kirillov dimension (Theorem 1.6)
items.statement: Let π be an admissible smooth representation of I/Z1 over F such that, for each character χ with Hom_I(χ, π) ≠ 0, the injection Hom_I(χ, π) ↪ Hom_I(W_{χ,3}, π) is an isomorphism. Then dim_I(π) = dim_{I/Z1}(π) ≤ f. (Theorem 1.6 states the same with multiplicities [π[m³_{I1/Z1}] : χ].)
items.note: Statement from the paper's own formulation; hypotheses abbreviated as in §1.2 and §8.1.

items.name: Connected semisimple representations of the Iwahori
items.statement: A semisimple smooth representation V of I over F is connected if any two distinct characters in V are joined by a chain of characters of V with consecutive members linked as in Definition 6.4.2.
items.note: Statement from the paper's own formulation; hypotheses abbreviated as in §1.2 and §8.1.

items.name: Multiplicity one for the pro-p Iwahori (Theorem 1.5)
items.statement: If π is admissible smooth over F with a central character satisfying (i) and (ii) of Theorem 6.4.7, then [π[m^3_{I1/Z1}] : χ] = [π[m_{I1/Z1}] : χ] for every character χ of I with [π[m_{I1/Z1}] : χ] ≠ 0.
items.note: Statement from the paper's own formulation; hypotheses abbreviated as in §1.2 and §8.1.

items.name: Local criterion for Gelfand–Kirillov dimension f (Theorem 1.4)
items.statement: Let ρ̄ be tame with ρ̄|_I ≅ τ(s, μ), μ − η 8-deep in C_0, and π an admissible smooth GL2(L)-representation over F with a central character such that (i) JH(soc_K π) = W(ρ̄), (ii) [π[m_{K1}²] : σ] = [soc_K π : σ] for σ ∈ W(ρ̄), and (iii) JH(π^{I1}) = JH(D_1(ρ̄)), all up to multiplicity. Then dim_{GL2(L)}(π) ≤ f. (Theorem 1.4 is the special case with π^{K1} ≅ D_0(r̄_v^∨)^{⊕r} and the multiplicity condition (ii).)
items.note: This is the introduction form; the slightly stronger conclusion of Theorem 6.4.7 is to be copied in the next continuation.

items.name: The lattices L_j and projective envelopes (Theorem 1.7)
items.statement: For the K-stable lattices L_j of §7.3 there is a K-equivariant isomorphism L_{f−1}/pL_{f−1} ≅ (Proj_{K/Z1} σ)/m^2_{K1/Z1}.
items.note: Statement from the paper's own formulation; hypotheses abbreviated as in §1.2 and §8.1.

items.name: N-generic Galois representations and tame types
items.statement: Tame inertial types are parametrized by pairs (s, μ) ∈ W × X*(T) (Definition 2.3.1); a tame type (Definition 2.3.3) and a representation ρ: G_K → GL_n(F) (Definition 2.3.4) are N-generic when the relevant exponents avoid a neighbourhood of size N of the walls.
items.note: Genericity conditions paraphrased; exact inequalities to be copied in the next continuation.

items.name: Kisin modules with tame descent data and the monodromy condition
items.statement: Kisin modules of height in [0, h] with descent data of tame type τ, their gauge bases and the monodromy condition, as in Definitions 3.1.1–3.1.8.
items.note: Statement from the paper's own formulation; hypotheses abbreviated as in §1.2 and §8.1.

items.name: Potentially Barsotti–Tate deformation rings for one and several tame types
items.statement: The framed deformation rings of ρ̄ with Hodge–Tate weights ≤ (3,0) have the explicit presentations of Proposition 4.2.1 (one tame type τ_w̃) and Proposition 4.3.1 (all types meeting a Serre weight σ), and each R_ρ̄^{λ,τ_w̃} has reduced special fibre with formally smooth components (Corollary 4.2.6).
items.note: Umbrella for §§4.2–4.3; the numbered statements are the items named as prerequisites. Statement from v7 read by cc-442dc5; notation as in the paper's §2 and the section named in the locator.

items.name: The patching functor M∞
items.statement: Fix tame types τ_w at w ∈ S_p∖{v} with exactly one Serre weight of W(r̄_w^∨) in JH(σ(τ_w)^∨) and lattices σ°(τ_w^∨); with σ_p^v = ⊗_w σ°(τ_w^∨) (62), the patching functor M∞: σ_v ↦ M∞(σ_p^v ⊗ σ_v) sends continuous representations of GL2(O_{F_v}) on finite type W(F)-modules with central character ψ|^{−1} to finite type R∞-modules, R∞ = R^loc[[X_1, …, X_{q−[F:Q]+|S|−1}]], following [EGS15, §§6.2, 6.4].
items.note: Statement from the paper's own formulation; hypotheses abbreviated as in §1.2 and §8.1.

items.name: Freeness of M∞(L_j) (Theorem 1.8)
items.statement: For j ∈ {−1, …, f − 1}, M∞(L_j) is free of finite rank over R∞/Ann_{R∞}(M∞(L_j)), and the rank depends neither on j nor on the Serre weight σ ∈ W(r_v^∨).
items.locator: arXiv:2009.03127v7 (final version), Theorem 8.3.9, p. 101; Theorem 1.8 (introduction form, cited there as 'Corollary 8.3.9', see E1)
items.note: Statement from the paper's own formulation; hypotheses abbreviated as in §1.2 and §8.1.

items.name: Structure of π[m^2_{K1/Z1}] (Theorem 1.9)
items.note: Statement from the paper's own formulation; hypotheses abbreviated as in §1.2 and §8.1.

items.name: Gelfand–Kirillov dimension of the patched representation (Theorem 1.10)
items.statement: For π as in (2), dim_{GL2(Fv)}(π) = f.
items.note: Statement from the paper's own formulation; hypotheses abbreviated as in §1.2 and §8.1.

items.name: Gelfand–Kirillov dimension of mod p cohomology of Shimura curves (Theorem 1.1)
items.statement: Assume r is generic and r|G_{F(ζ_p)} is absolutely irreducible, with level V = ∏_{w≠v} V_w as in §1.2. Then for π as in (1), the r-part of the mod p cohomology of Shimura curves at infinite level at v, dim_{GL2(Fv)}(π) = f.
items.note: Statement from the paper's own formulation; hypotheses abbreviated as in §1.2 and §8.1.

items.name: Banach lifts (Theorem 1.3)
items.statement: Under Theorem 1.1's hypotheses, for any x: R∞ → O′, Hom_cont(M∞ ⊗_{R∞,x} O′, E′) is a nonzero admissible unitary Banach representation of GL2(Fv) with an invariant unit ball lifting π ⊗_F F′.
items.note: Statement from the paper's own formulation; hypotheses abbreviated as in §1.2 and §8.1.

items.name: Flatness of the dual of completed cohomology (Theorem 1.2)
items.statement: There is an isomorphism R_{r,S} → T̂(V^v)_{m_r}; the dual of completed H^1 localized at r is faithfully flat over T̂(V^v)_{m_r}, which is a complete intersection.
items.note: Notation abbreviated; copy the exact module and fixed-character conventions of §8.5 in the next continuation.

items.name: The tame inertial type τ(s, μ + η)
items.statement: Fix (s, μ) ∈ W × X*(T). Write s = (s_0, …, s_{f−1}) ∈ W, set s_τ = s_0 s_{f−1} s_{f−2} ⋯ s_1 ∈ S_n and let r be the order of s_τ; put f′ = rf and e′ = p^{f′} − 1. Let K′/K be the unramified extension of degree r with residue field k′, fix an embedding σ′_0 : k′ ↪ F extending σ_0 and identify 𝒥′ = Hom(k′, F) with {0, …, f′ − 1} by σ′_{j′} = σ′_0 ∘ φ^{j′} ↦ j′. Let ω_{f′} : I_K → F^× be the tame fundamental character, the composite I_K = I_{K′} ↠ O_{K′}^× ↠ k′^× → F^× whose first map is the local Artin map normalized so that uniformizers correspond to geometric Frobenius elements, and let ω̃_{f′} : I_K → O^× be its Teichmüller lift. Define α′_{(s,μ),j′} = s_1^{-1} s_2^{-1} ⋯ s_{j′}^{-1}(μ_{j′} + η_{j′}) ∈ Z^n for j′ ∈ Z (indices mod f), so that α′_{(s,μ),j′+kf} = s_τ^{−k} α′_{(s,μ),j′}, and set a′^{(j′)}_{(s,μ)} = Σ_{i′=0}^{f′−1} α′_{(s,μ),−j′+i′} p^{i′} ∈ Z^n. Then τ(s, μ + η) = ⊕_{1≤i≤n} ω̃_{f′}^{a′^{(0)}_{(s,μ),i}} : I_K → GL_n(O). Equivalently, with a^{(0)} = Σ_{j=0}^{f−1} α′_{(s,μ),j} p^j, τ(s, μ + η) = ⊕_{1≤i≤n} ω̃_{f′}^{Σ_{0≤k≤r−1} a^{(0)}_{s_τ^k(i)} p^{fk}}. It is a tame inertial type, i.e. extends to G_K; τ̄(s, μ + η) denotes its reduction mod ϖ.
items.locator: arXiv:2009.03127v7 (final version), §2.3, Definition 2.3.1 with (11) and (12), p. 14
items.note: Checked on a page image. Remark 2.3.2 warns that, because the embeddings of k in F are labelled by σ_j = σ_0 ∘ φ^j here, this definition is not compatible with [LLHL19, Def. 2.2.1], a choice made for compatibility with [Her09] and [GHS18].

items.name: N-generic tame inertial types and lowest alcove presentations
items.statement: Let τ be a tame inertial type and N ∈ Z_{≥0}. (i) τ is N-generic if τ ≅ τ(s, λ + η) for some s ∈ W and λ ∈ X*(T) which is N-deep in the alcove C̲_0. (ii) A lowest alcove presentation of τ is a pair (s, μ) ∈ W × C̲_0 with τ ≅ τ(s, μ + η).
items.note: Remark 2.3.5: if τ is N-generic and (s, λ) is a lowest alcove presentation, λ need not be N-deep in C̲_0, but is (N−1)-deep by [LLHL19, Prop. 2.2.16].

items.name: N-generic Galois representations
items.statement: Let ρ̄ : G_K → GL_n(F) and N ∈ N. Writing ρ̄^{ss}|_{I_K} for the restriction to inertia of the semisimplification, ρ̄ is N-generic if ρ̄^{ss}|_{I_K} ≅ τ̄(s, μ) for some s ∈ W and μ − η ∈ X*(T) which is N-deep in C̲_0.
items.note: The paper notes the shift of convention: what is written μ here was μ + η in Definition 2.3.1.

items.name: The orientation s′_or of a lowest alcove presentation
items.statement: For a lowest alcove presentation (s, μ), the orientation s′_or ∈ (S_n)^{Hom(k′,F)} ≅ W^r of α′_{(s,μ)} is defined by s′_{or,j′} = s_1^{-1} ⋯ s_{j′}^{-1} (with the convention of §2.3). If μ ∈ X*(T) is 0-deep in C̲_0 then s′_{or,j′} is the unique element of W for which (s′_{or,j′})^{-1}(α′^{(j′)}_{(s,μ)}) ∈ X*(T) is dominant, and (s′_{or,−j′})^{-1}(α′_{(s,μ),j′}) = s_{j′}^{-1}(μ_{j′} + η_{j′}).
items.locator: arXiv:2009.03127v7 (final version), §2.3, Remarks 2.3.5 and 2.3.6 with (13), p. 15
items.note: The orientation is the bookkeeping device used throughout §3 to normalize the matrices of a Kisin module; it is not stated as a numbered result in the paper.

items.name: The lattices Λ_W, Λ_R, Λ_W^μ, the map t_μ and the set Σ
items.statement: Λ_W = X*(T)/X^0(T) with its natural inclusion Λ_R ↪ Λ_W, identified with (2Z)^𝒥 ⊆ Z^𝒥 under Λ_W ≅ Z^𝒥. For μ ∈ X*(T), Λ_W^μ ⊆ Λ_W is the subset defined in §2.1 and t_μ : Λ_W^μ → X*(T)/(p − π)X^0(T) is the induced map, with image in X_reg(T)/(p − π)X^0(T). In coordinates: if μ = (a_j, b_j)_j ∈ X*(T) and ω = (2n_j + δ_j)_j ∈ Λ_W^μ with n_j ∈ Z and δ_j ∈ {0,1}, then a representative of t_μ(ω) is (t_μ(ω))_j = (a_j + n_j + δ_j, b_j − n_j) if δ_{j+1} = 0, and (b_j − 1 − n_j, a_j + n_j + δ_j − p + 1) if δ_{j+1} = 1. For J ⊆ 𝒥 put η_J = Σ_{j∈J} η_j ∈ X*(T) and let η̄_J be its image in Λ_W; Σ ⊆ Λ_W is the set {η̄_J : J ⊆ 𝒥}.
items.locator: arXiv:2009.03127v7 (final version), §2.4, (14) and the paragraph before Proposition 2.4.2, p. 16
items.note: Checked on a page image. Remark 2.4.1: in [LMS22, §2.2] Λ_W^μ is written Λ_W^{μ+η} and t_μ is written t_{μ+η}.

items.name: Proposition 2.4.2 — the Serre weights of a tame ρ̄
items.statement: Suppose ρ̄ : G_K → GL_2(F) is tame with ρ̄|_{I_K} ≅ τ̄(s, μ) for some (s, μ) ∈ W × X*(T) with μ − η lying 1-deep in C̲_0. Then W(ρ̄) = {F(t_{μ−η}(sω)) : ω ∈ Σ}.
items.note: Checked on a page image. W(ρ̄) is the set of Serre weights of Buzzard–Diamond–Jarvis [BDJ10, §3]; the proof identifies the right-hand side with W_obv(ρ̄) of [GHS18, Def. 7.1.3] and quotes [GHS18, Ex. 7.1.7]. The cited inputs were not read.

items.name: Proposition 2.4.3 — the Jordan–Hölder factors of σ̄(τ)
items.statement: Suppose τ = τ(sw^{-1}, μ − sw^{-1}(ν)) for some (s, μ), (w, ν) ∈ W × X*(T) with μ − sw^{-1}(ν) − η lying 1-deep in C̲_0. If ν ∈ η + Λ_R, then JH(σ̄(τ)) = {F(t_{μ−η}(sw^{-1}(ω − ν̄))) : ω ∈ Σ}.
items.note: Checked on a page image. σ(τ) is the GL_2(O_K)-type attached to τ by inertial local Langlands and σ̄(τ) its reduction; the proof quotes [LLHL19, Cor. 2.3.5] and [DL21, Prop. 2.15], which were not read.

items.name: Lemma 2.4.4 — change of origin for t_μ
items.statement: Let ω ∈ Λ_W^μ and λ ∈ X*(T) with t_μ(ω) ≡ λ mod (p − π)X^0(T). Then w_ω^{-1}(ω′) + ω ∈ Λ_W^μ and t_λ(ω′) = t_μ(w_ω^{-1}(ω′) + ω) for all ω′ ∈ Λ_W^λ; equivalently t_μ(ω′) = t_λ(w_ω(ω′ − ω)) for ω′ ∈ Λ_W^μ.
items.note: Obtained from [LMS22, Prop. 2.5]. Remark 2.4.5 records that w_ω = w_{0,J} when ω ≡ η_J mod Λ_R, and that w_ν = 1 for ν ∈ Λ_R. Remark 2.4.7: the change-of-origin map Λ_W^λ → Λ_W^μ preserves adjacency, and under Λ_W ≅ Z^𝒥 has the form (a_0, …, a_{f−1}) ↦ (ε_0a_0 + n_0, …, ε_{f−1}a_{f−1} + n_{f−1}) with ε_i ∈ {±1}, n_i ∈ Z.

items.name: Lemma 2.4.6 — extensions between Serre weights
items.statement: For ω, ω′ ∈ Λ_W^μ, dim_F Ext^1_{GL_2(k)}(F(t_μ(ω)), F(t_μ(ω′))) = 1 if ω and ω′ are adjacent and 0 otherwise.
items.note: Adjacency is the graph structure on Λ_W^μ ≅ Z^𝒥 recalled in §2.4. This is what makes the combinatorics of §6 a graph problem.

items.name: Definition 3.1.1 — the matrices C_{M,β} and A_{M,β}
items.statement: For a Kisin module M ∈ Y^{[0,h],τ}(R) with eigenbasis β, C^{(j′)}_{M,β} ∈ M_n(R⟦u′⟧) is the matrix of φ*(M^{(j′)}) → M^{(j′+1)} in the bases φ*(β^{(j′)}) and β^{(j′+1)}, i.e. β^{(j′+1)}C^{(j′)}_{M,β} = φ^{(j′)}_M(φ*(β^{(j′)})), and A^{(j′)}_{M,β} ∈ M_n(R⟦v⟧) is A^{(j′)}_{M,β} = Ad((ṡ′_{or,j′+1})^{−1} (u′)^{−a′^{(j′+1)}_{(s,μ)}})(C^{(j′)}_{M,β}) (cf. [LLHLM23, (5.4)], where C^{(j′)} denotes the matrix of φ*(M^{(j′−1)}) → M^{(j′)}).
items.note: Remark 3.1.2 cautions that Ad(ṡ(u′)^μ) means Ad(ṡ)Ad((u′)^μ), not Ad((u′)^{s(μ)}), where ṡ is the permutation matrix of s and (u′)^μ = Diag((u′)^{μ_1}, …, (u′)^{μ_n}). Remark 3.1.3: the notions of eigenbasis and of A_{M,β} depend on the chosen lowest alcove presentation (s, μ) of τ; since μ is 1-deep in C̲_0, A^{(j′)}_{M,β} depends only on j′ mod f and is upper triangular modulo v. (cc-442dc5) The display of Definition 3.1.1 is transcribed from the page image of p. 18.

items.name: Definition 3.1.4 — the shape of a Kisin module
items.statement: Let M̄ ∈ Y^{[0,h],τ}(F) and let I(F) be the Iwahori subgroup of GL_n(F⟦v⟧) of matrices upper triangular modulo v. M̄ has shape w̃ ∈ W̃^∨ with respect to τ if for any eigenbasis β̄ of M̄ the equality I(F) A^{(j)}_{M̄,β̄} I(F) = I(F) w̃_j I(F) holds in GL_n(F((v))) for all j = 0, …, f − 1.
items.note: Checked on a page image. The notion is independent of β̄ by [LLHLM18, Prop. 2.15, 2.16], but again depends on the chosen lowest alcove presentation of τ.

items.name: Proposition 3.1.5 — existence and uniqueness of a gauge basis
items.statement: Let R be a complete noetherian local O-algebra with residue field F and let τ be an (h+1)-generic tame inertial type. Let M ∈ Y^{[0,h],τ}(R) with an isomorphism M ⊗_R F ≅ M̄. Then there is an eigenbasis β of M lifting β̄ such that for all 1 ≤ i, k ≤ n and all j = 0, …, f − 1: (i) A^{(j)}_{ik} ∈ v^{δ_{i>k}} R[v + p]; (ii) deg_v(A^{(j)}_{ik}) ≤ ν_{j,k} − δ_{i<w_j(k)}, with equality if (i, k) = (w_j(k), k); where A^{(j)} = A^{(j)}_{M,β}, δ_{i>k} ∈ {0,1} is 1 exactly when i > k, and δ_{i<w_j(k)} ∈ {0,1} is 1 exactly when i < w_j(k). Such a β is unique up to scaling by {(t_j)_{j∈𝒥′} ∈ (ker(T(R) → T(F)))^{f′} : t_j = t_k for j ≡ k mod f}.
items.note: Checked on a page image. Here w̃ = (w_j t_{ν_j})_j ∈ W̃^∨ is the shape of M̄ with respect to τ, fixed together with a gauge basis β̄ of M̄ before the statement. The result generalizes [LLHLM18, Thm. 4.1, 4.16] and [LLHL19, Prop. 3.4.3] and is a particular case of [LLHLM23, Prop. 5.2.7], which was not read.

items.name: Definition 3.1.6 — gauge basis
items.statement: For R a complete noetherian local O-algebra with residue field F and M ∈ Y^{[0,h],τ}(R) with M ⊗_R F ≅ M̄, a gauge basis of M is an eigenbasis β lifting β̄ satisfying conditions (i) and (ii) of Proposition 3.1.5.
items.note: For M̄ itself the notion of gauge basis is recalled from [LLHL19, Def. 3.2.23]: a gauge basis always exists and is unique up to scaling by {(t_j)_{j∈𝒥′} ∈ T(F)^{f′} : t_j = t_k for j ≡ k mod f}.

items.name: Proposition 3.1.7 — the monodromy derivation
items.statement: Let M ∈ Y^{[0,h],τ}(R) for R a p-adically complete flat O-algebra topologically of finite type. Then M^rig[1/λ] carries a unique derivation N_{M^rig} over N_∇ with N_{M^rig} φ_{M^rig} = E(u′) φ_{M^rig} N_{M^rig} and N_{M^rig} ≡ 0 mod u′, compatibly with the decomposition into the components M^{rig,(j′)}.

items.name: Definition 3.1.8 — the monodromy condition
items.statement: For M ∈ Y^{[0,h],τ}(R) with eigenbasis β, the monodromy condition is that λ^{h−1} N^{(j′)}_{M^rig,β} vanishes to order h − 1 at u′ = (−p)^{1/e} for every j′. It is equivalent to N_{M^rig}(M^rig) ⊆ M^rig.
items.note: The equivalence is seen as in [LLHLM18, Prop. 5.3].

items.name: Proposition 3.1.9 — the monodromy condition in coordinates
items.statement: Let M ∈ Y^{[0,h],τ}(R) with eigenbasis β. The monodromy condition is equivalent to (d/du′)^t |_{u′=(−p)^{1/e′}} [ Ad((s′_{or,j′})^{-1}(u′)^{−a′^{(j′)}_{(s,μ)}}) (λ^{h−1} N^{(j′)}_{M^rig,β}) ] = 0 for all t = 0, …, h − 2 and j′ = 0, …, f′ − 1, and depends only on j′ mod f. If moreover τ is N-generic with N ≥ 2h − 3 and (N−1)(p−1) ≥ h, the condition takes the form (d/dv)^t |_{v=−p} (P_N(A^{(j−1)}_{M,β})) + O(p^{N−(h−1)−t}) = 0 for all j = 0, …, f − 1 and t = 0, …, h − 2, where P_N(A^{(j−1)}_{M,β}) = (−e′ v (d/dv) A^{(j−1)}_{M,β} − [Diag((s′_{or,j})^{-1}(a′^{(j)}_{(s,μ)})), A^{(j−1)}_{M,β}]) (v+p)^h (A^{(j−1)}_{M,β})^{-1} is the leading term of the monodromy condition, and the terms O(p^{N−(h−1)−t}) are specific but inexplicit elements of p^{N−(h−1)−t} M_2(R).
items.locator: arXiv:2009.03127v7 (final version), §3.1.2, Proposition 3.1.9 with (16) and (17), p. 21
items.note: Checked on a page image. Attributed to [LLHLM18]; the proof is a generalization of [LLHL19, Prop. 3.4.12], the case h = n − 1, N = 2n − 1. The leading term P_N is what the explicit presentations of the deformation rings in §4 are computed from.

items.name: Definition 3.2.1 — good pairs (s, μ)
items.statement: (s, μ) ∈ W × X*(T) is good if Σ_{j=0}^{fd(i)−1} p^j (s_1^{-1} ⋯ s_j^{-1}(μ_j))_i ≢ 0 mod (q^{d(i)} − 1)/(q^d − 1) for all 1 ≤ i ≤ n and all d | d(i) with 1 ≤ d < d(i), where d(i) ≥ 1 is minimal with s_1^{-1}s_2^{-1} ⋯ s_{fd(i)}^{-1}(i) = i and the indices are taken modulo f.
items.note: Generalizes [Her09, Def. 6.19]. Remark 3.2.2: τ(s, μ) is the restriction to I_K of an irreducible n-dimensional representation of G_K if and only if s_τ has order n and (s, μ) is good.

items.name: Lemma 3.2.3 — deep pairs are good
items.statement: If μ − η ∈ C̲_0 then (s, μ) is good for every s ∈ W.

items.name: Definition 3.2.4 — the étale φ-module M(w̃, D)
items.statement: For w̃ ∈ W̃^∨ and D ∈ T(F), M(w̃, D) is the étale φ-module free of rank n over k((v)) ⊗_{F_p} F with Mat(φ^{(j)}) = D_j w̃_j ∈ GL_n(F((v))) with respect to the standard basis, where W̃^∨ embeds into GL_n(F((v)))^f as at the end of §2.1.

items.name: Definition 3.2.5 — the tame representation V(w̃, D)
items.statement: For w̃ ∈ W̃^∨ and D ∈ T(F), V(w̃, D) is the unique tame representation of G_K over F of dimension n with V(w̃, D)|_{G_{K_∞}} ≅ V*_{K_∞}(M(w̃, D)).
items.note: Existence and uniqueness are guaranteed by [LLHL19, Prop. 3.1.2] and the equivalence for tame representations in [LLHL19, §3.1].

items.name: Lemma 3.2.6 — unramified twists of V(w̃, D)
items.statement: For λ ∈ (F^×)^f, V(w̃, λD) ≅ V(w̃, D) ⊗_F nr(∏_{j=0}^{f−1} λ_j), where nr(α) is the unramified character of G_K sending an arithmetic Frobenius to α ∈ F^×.

items.name: Proposition 3.2.7 — tame representations with a given type
items.statement: Let w̃ ∈ W̃^∨ and suppose w̃* = t_{μ′} s′ ∈ W̃ is such that (s′, μ′) ∈ W × X*(T) is good. Then {ρ : G_K → GL_n(F) semisimple : ρ|_{I_K} ≅ τ̄(s′, μ′)}/≅ = {V(w̃, D) : D ∈ T(F)}/≅.
items.note: The proof uses [LLHL19, Prop. 3.1.2] for V(w̃, D)|_{I_K} ≅ τ̄(s′, μ′) and then shows both that V(w̃, D) is semisimple and that the left side is contained in the right; the cited input was not read.

items.name: Lemma 3.2.8 — restriction to G_{K_∞} on homomorphisms
items.statement: If ρ_1, ρ_2 are finite-dimensional representations of G_K over F such that ρ_1^∨ ⊗_F ρ_2 is cyclotomic free, then the natural map Hom_{G_K}(ρ_1, ρ_2) → Hom_{G_{K_∞}}(ρ_1|_{G_{K_∞}}, ρ_2|_{G_{K_∞}}) is an isomorphism.

items.name: Corollary 3.2.9 — isomorphisms descend from G_{K_∞}
items.statement: If ρ_1, ρ_2 are finite-dimensional representations of G_K over F with ρ_1 2-generic, then the natural injective map Isom_{G_K}(ρ_1, ρ_2) → Isom_{G_{K_∞}}(ρ_1|_{G_{K_∞}}, ρ_2|_{G_{K_∞}}) is a bijection.
items.note: This is what lets the paper work with Kisin modules, i.e. over G_{K_∞}, without losing information about G_K.

items.name: Lemma 3.3.1 — irreducibility of x_1x_2 + ϖ^d f
items.statement: Let A = O⟦x_1, …, x_n⟧ with O a complete DVR with uniformizer ϖ and n ≥ 2. If f ∈ A^× and d > 0 then x_1x_2 + ϖ^d f is irreducible in A. Moreover the ideals (x_1x_2 + ϖ^d f) and (x_1) are distinct, and (x_1x_2 + ϖ^d f_1) and (x_1x_2 + ϖ^d f_2) are distinct if f_1 ≢ f_2 mod m_A.
items.note: A commutative-algebra lemma, used in §4 to identify the components of the deformation rings; the only statement of the paper that is not about representations.

items.name: Lemma 4.1.1 — the semisimple Kisin module of shape w̃
items.statement: For ρ̄ and w̃ ∈ Adm^∨(t_(2,1)) as in §4.1, there is up to isomorphism a unique (semisimple) Kisin module M in Y^{≤(3,0),τ_w̃}(F) of shape w̃ with T*_dd(M) ≅ ρ̄|_{G_{K∞}}.
items.note: Statement from v7 read by cc-442dc5; notation as in the paper's §2 and the section named in the locator.

items.name: Lemma 4.1.2 — the bijection θ between Serre weights and shapes
items.statement: There is a unique bijection θ: W(ρ̄) → {t_(2,1), t_(1,2)}^f such that σ ∈ JH(σ(τ_w̃) ⊗ (N_{k/F_p} ∘ det)) if and only if w̃_j ≠ θ(σ)_j for all j (20). Moreover JH(σ(τ) ⊗ (N ∘ det)) ∩ W(ρ̄) ≠ ∅ for a tame type τ if and only if τ = τ_w̃ for some w̃ ∈ Adm^∨(t_(2,1)).
items.note: Statement from v7 read by cc-442dc5; notation as in the paper's §2 and the section named in the locator.

items.name: Proposition 4.2.1 — presentation of the single-type deformation ring
items.statement: R_ρ̄^{≤(3,0),τ_w̃}[[X_1, …, X_2f]] ≅ R/Σ_j I^(j) [[Y_1, …, Y_4]], with R the completed tensor product of the O-algebras R^(j) and the ideals I^(j) of Tables 1–3. The irreducible components of Spec R_ρ̄^{≤(3,0),τ_w̃} are the Spec R_ρ̄^{λ,τ_w̃} for λ ∈ {(3,0),(2,1)}^f, and the kernel of the surjection onto R_ρ̄^{λ,τ_w̃}[[X]] is generated by the prime ideal Σ_j p^{(j),λ_{f−1−j}} of Tables 1–3.
items.note: The rings and ideals are those of Tables 1–3 of the paper and are not transcribed here. Statement from v7 read by cc-442dc5; notation as in the paper's §2 and the section named in the locator.

items.name: Lemma 4.2.3 — p³ lies in H^(j) + I_poly
items.statement: With the notation of the proof of Proposition 4.2.1, p³ ∈ H^(j) + I_poly.
items.note: Statement from v7 read by cc-442dc5; notation as in the paper's §2 and the section named in the locator.

items.name: Lemma 4.2.4 — comparison of the polynomial and ∞-approximations
items.statement: There is an automorphism of local O-algebras ψ: R → R compatible with an isomorphism R/I_poly ≅ R/I_∞ and inducing the identity modulo p^{N−8}.
items.note: Statement from v7 read by cc-442dc5; notation as in the paper's §2 and the section named in the locator.

items.name: Corollary 4.2.6 — reduced special fibres
items.statement: For each λ ∈ {(3,0),(2,1)}^f and w̃ ∈ Adm^∨(t_(2,1)), the special fibre of Spec R_ρ̄^{λ,τ_w̃} is reduced and all its irreducible components are formally smooth over F.
items.note: Statement from v7 read by cc-442dc5; notation as in the paper's §2 and the section named in the locator.

items.name: Proposition 4.3.1 — presentation of the multi-type deformation ring
items.statement: For σ ∈ W(ρ̄) and X(σ) = {w̃ ∈ Adm^∨(t_(2,1)) : w̃_j ≠ θ(σ)_j ∀ j}, R_ρ̄^{≤(3,0),σ}[[X_1, …, X_2f]] ≅ S/(∩_{w̃∈X(σ)} Σ_j I_w̃^(j))[[Y_1, …, Y_4]] with S and the ideals of Tables 4–5; the irreducible components are the Spec R_ρ̄^{λ,τ_w̃} for λ ∈ {(3,0),(2,1)}^f and w̃ ∈ X(σ), cut out by the prime ideals Σ_j p_w̃^{(j),λ} of Tables 4–5.
items.note: The rings and ideals are those of Tables 4–5 of the paper and are not transcribed here. Statement from v7 read by cc-442dc5; notation as in the paper's §2 and the section named in the locator.

items.name: Lemma 4.3.2 — the ideals q_i^{(j),(2,1)}
items.statement: For the ideals q_1, q_2 (if (w̃_σ)_{f−1−j} = t_(1,2)) and q_2, q_3 (if = t_(2,1)) of S^(j) defined in the lemma, q_{i(w̃)_{f−1−j}}^{(j),(2,1)} ⊆ Σ_{j′} p_w̃^{(j′),λ_{f−1−j′}} whenever λ_{f−1−j} = (2,1), and Σ_{j′} q_{i(w̃)_{f−1−j′}}^{(j′),(2,1)} = Σ_{j′} p_w̃^{(j′),(2,1)} as ideals of S.
items.note: The generators of the q-ideals are displayed in the lemma and are not transcribed here. Statement from v7 read by cc-442dc5; notation as in the paper's §2 and the section named in the locator.

items.name: Proposition 4.3.3 — p lies in the intersected ideals
items.note: Statement from v7 read by cc-442dc5; notation as in the paper's §2 and the section named in the locator.

items.name: Lemma 5.1.2 — GK dimension through a trivially acting normal subgroup
items.statement: If N is a closed normal subgroup of a p-adic analytic group G acting trivially on an admissible smooth F-representation π, then dim_G(π) = dim_{G/N}(π).
items.note: Statement from v7 read by cc-442dc5; notation as in the paper's §2 and the section named in the locator.

items.name: Lemma 5.1.3 — GK dimension via a central regular sequence
items.statement: Let G be an analytic pro-p group without p-torsion with gr_m F[[G]] Auslander-regular, and I a two-sided ideal generated by a gr_m F[[G]]-regular sequence of r central elements with gr_m F[[G]]/I a polynomial ring in dim(G) − r variables. If M is a finitely generated F[[G]]-module with gr_m M killed by I, then dim_G(M) is the dimension of the support of gr_m M in Spec(gr_m F[[G]]/I).
items.note: Statement from v7 read by cc-442dc5; notation as in the paper's §2 and the section named in the locator.

items.name: Lemma 5.3.1 — the p-valued Lie algebra of G
items.statement: L_G ≅ O_L ⊗_{Z_p} g_{Z_p} as p-valued Lie algebras, with w([[pa, b], [pc, −pa]]) = min{1 + v_p(a), 1/2 + v_p(b), 1/2 + v_p(c)} (38).
items.note: Statement from v7 read by cc-442dc5; notation as in the paper's §2 and the section named in the locator.

items.name: Lemma 5.3.2 — congruences in F_p[[G]]
items.statement: For a pro-p group G and g, h ∈ G: gh − 1 ≡ (g − 1) + (h − 1) and g^{−1} − 1 ≡ −(g − 1) modulo m_G², and g^p − 1 ∈ m_G^p.
items.note: Statement from v7 read by cc-442dc5; notation as in the paper's §2 and the section named in the locator.

items.name: Proposition 5.3.3 — the m-adic filtration is the valuation filtration
items.note: Statement from v7 read by cc-442dc5; notation as in the paper's §2 and the section named in the locator.

items.name: The representations W_{χ,n} of the Iwahori
items.statement: For a smooth character χ: I → F^× and n ≥ 1, W_{χ,n} = (Proj_{I/Z1} χ)/m_{I1}^n (45).
items.note: Statement from v7 read by cc-442dc5; notation as in the paper's §2 and the section named in the locator.

items.name: Lemma 6.1.1 — extensions of Iwahori characters
items.statement: (i) [W_{χ,3} : χ′] ≤ 1 for χ′ ≠ χ. (ii) If Ext¹_{I/Z1}(χ, χ′) ≠ 0 then χ′ ∈ {χα_i^{±1}} and the Ext is one-dimensional; the nonsplit extension E_{χ′,χ} is trivial on K1 exactly when χ′ = χα_i.
items.note: Statement from v7 read by cc-442dc5; notation as in the paper's §2 and the section named in the locator.

items.name: Lemma 6.1.2 — injectivity of maps W_{χ′,2} → W_{χ,3}
items.statement: If Ext¹_{I/Z1}(χ, χ′) ≠ 0, every nonzero I-equivariant morphism W_{χ′,2} → W_{χ,3} is injective.
items.note: Statement from v7 read by cc-442dc5; notation as in the paper's §2 and the section named in the locator.

items.name: Lemma 6.1.3 — the injective envelope of a character of B(k)
items.statement: I_χ = Inj_{B(k)} χ has socle and cosocle χ, its other Jordan–Hölder factors χα_0^{−j} (0 < j < q − 1) have multiplicity one, and the unique proper submodule with cosocle χα_0^{−j} has factors χα_0^{−ℓ} with ℓ_i ≤ j_i for all digits i.
items.note: Statement from v7 read by cc-442dc5; notation as in the paper's §2 and the section named in the locator.

items.name: Corollary 6.1.4 — the representation J_χ
items.statement: For χ: T(k) → F^× there is a finite-dimensional smooth I-representation J_χ with a central character, socle and cosocle χ^s, other factors χ^s α_0^j (0 < j < q − 1) of multiplicity one, with the submodule structure of Lemma 6.1.3.
items.note: Statement from v7 read by cc-442dc5; notation as in the paper's §2 and the section named in the locator.

items.name: Lemma 6.2.1 — constituents of principal series and injective envelopes
items.statement: (i) If 0 < ⟨λ, α_i^∨⟩ < p − 1 then Ind_I^K χ_λ^s is multiplicity-free with factors F(t_λ(−η_J)), J ⊆ 𝒥. (ii) If 0 < ⟨λ, α_i^∨⟩ < p − 2, the factors of Inj_{GL2(k)} F(λ) are the F(t_λ(Σ a_i η_i)) with a_i ∈ {0, ±1}. (iii) Under (ii), the factors of I(F(λ), σ′) for σ′ = F(t_λ(Σ a_i η_i)) are F(t_λ(Σ_{i∈J} a_i η_i)), J ⊆ 𝒥, so its length is 2^{|{i : a_i ≠ 0}|}.
items.note: Statement from v7 read by cc-442dc5; notation as in the paper's §2 and the section named in the locator.

items.name: Proposition 6.2.2 — multiplicity-free representations with prescribed structure
items.statement: For λ, B_i ≥ 0 and ε_i ∈ {±1} satisfying the parity and bound conditions (i)–(iii), there is a multiplicity-free K/Z1-representation V with constituents σ_a = F(t_λ(Σ ε_i a_i η_i)), 0 ≤ a_i ≤ B_i, whose subrepresentation with cosocle σ_a has constituents σ_b for 0 ≤ b ≤ a; its socle is F(λ).
items.note: Statement from v7 read by cc-442dc5; notation as in the paper's §2 and the section named in the locator.

items.name: Lemma 6.2.3 — a criterion for K1-invariance
items.statement: A finite-dimensional smooth K-representation V with irreducible socle σ = F(λ), 2 < ⟨λ, α_i^∨⟩ < p − 3, [V : σ] = 1 and all constituents in Inj_{GL2(k)} σ is K1-invariant.
items.note: Statement from v7 read by cc-442dc5; notation as in the paper's §2 and the section named in the locator.

items.name: Proposition 6.2.4 — the m_{K1}-torsion filtration of V
items.statement: Under stronger bounds on λ, for the V of Proposition 6.2.2 and 0 ≤ n − 1 ≤ ⌊B_i/2⌋, V[m_{K1}^n] is the subrepresentation with cosocle ⊕σ_a over the a with 0 ≤ a_i ≤ B_i, a_i odd or a_i = B_i, and Σ ⌊a_i/2⌋ = n − 1.
items.note: Statement from v7 read by cc-442dc5; notation as in the paper's §2 and the section named in the locator.

items.name: Lemma 6.3.1 — cosocle of Ind_I^K E_{χ′,χ}
items.statement: If χ′ = χα_i^{−1}, the cosocle of Ind_I^K E_{χ′,χ} equals the cosocle of Ind_I^K χ.
items.note: Statement from v7 read by cc-442dc5; notation as in the paper's §2 and the section named in the locator.

items.name: Lemma 6.3.3 — multiplicity-freeness of Ind_I^K E and Ind_I^K W_{χ,2}
items.statement: If 0 < ⟨λ, α_i^∨⟩ < p − 3 for all i, Ind_I^K E_{χα_i,χ} is multiplicity-free; if moreover χ = χ_λ with 2 < ⟨λ, α_i^∨⟩ < p − 3, Ind_I^K W_{χ,2} is multiplicity-free.
items.note: The first sentence of the lemma leaves the relation between χ and λ implicit (χ = χ_λ). Statement from v7 read by cc-442dc5; notation as in the paper's §2 and the section named in the locator.

items.name: Lemma 6.3.4 — Jordan–Hölder factors of the image of f
items.statement: For χ = χ_λ with 0 < ⟨λ, α_i^∨⟩ < p − 3 and χ′ = χα_i, JH(Im(f)) = JH(Ind_I^K E_{χ′,χ}) ∩ JH(Proj_{GL2(k)} σ_χ) (47).
items.note: Statement from v7 read by cc-442dc5; notation as in the paper's §2 and the section named in the locator.

items.name: Lemma 6.3.5 — vanishing of Ext¹ against σ_χ
items.statement: Under Lemma 6.3.4's hypotheses, if Q is a quotient of Ind_I^K E_{χ′,χ} with [Q : σ_χ] = 0, then Ext¹_K(σ, σ_χ) = 0 for every σ ∈ JH(Q).
items.note: Statement from v7 read by cc-442dc5; notation as in the paper's §2 and the section named in the locator.

items.name: The representations D_{λ,ε}
items.statement: For ε ∈ {−1, 0, 1}^𝒥, D_{λ,ε} = I(F(λ), F(t_λ(Σ ε_i η_i))) (48), of length 2^{|J_ε|} with factors F(t_λ(Σ_{i∈J} ε_i η_i)), J ⊆ J_ε.
items.note: Statement from v7 read by cc-442dc5; notation as in the paper's §2 and the section named in the locator.

items.name: Lemma 6.3.7 — constituents of D_{λ,ε} ⊗ F(α_j)
items.statement: For 2 < ⟨λ, α_i^∨⟩ < p − 4, the factors of D_{λ,ε} ⊗ F(α_j) have multiplicity one and are F(t_λ(2ε′η_j + Σ_{i∈J} ε_i η_i)) for J ⊆ J_ε and ε′ ∈ {−1, 0, 1}.
items.note: Statement from v7 read by cc-442dc5; notation as in the paper's §2 and the section named in the locator.

items.name: Lemma 6.3.8 — socle and cosocle of D_{λ,ε} ⊗ F(α_j)
items.statement: Under Lemma 6.3.7, soc(D_{λ,ε} ⊗ F(α_j)) ≅ ⊕_{ε′} F(t_λ(2ε′η_j)) and cosoc ≅ ⊕_{ε′} F(t_λ(2ε′η_j + Σ_{i∈J_ε} ε_i η_i)).
items.note: Statement from v7 read by cc-442dc5; notation as in the paper's §2 and the section named in the locator.

items.name: Lemma 6.3.9 — the filtration of V ⊗ F(α_j)
items.statement: For λ 4-deep and V the nonsplit extension of F(t_λ(εη_j)) by F(λ), V ⊗ F(α_j) has a 3-step filtration with pieces the nonsplit extensions of F(t_λ(3εη_j)) by F(t_λ(2εη_j)), of F(t_λ(εη_j)) by F(λ), and of F(t_λ(−εη_j)) by F(t_λ(−2εη_j)), glued by nonsplit extensions as in the graph (50).
items.note: Statement from v7 read by cc-442dc5; notation as in the paper's §2 and the section named in the locator.

items.name: Proposition 6.3.10 — the filtration of D_{λ,ε} ⊗ F(α_j)
items.statement: For λ 4-deep and ε_j ≠ 0, D_{λ,ε} ⊗ F(α_j) has a 3-step filtration with pieces D_{λ+ε_jα_j,ε}, D_{λ,ε}, D_{λ−ε_jα_j,ε} (53); for λ 5-deep, whenever Ext¹(σ, σ′) ≠ 0 between constituents, one of the two nonsplit extensions occurs as a subquotient.
items.note: Statement from v7 read by cc-442dc5; notation as in the paper's §2 and the section named in the locator.

items.name: Theorem 6.3.11 — the largest subrepresentation W of Inj F(λ)[m_{K1}²]
items.statement: For λ 7-deep and ε ∈ {±1}^𝒥 there is a largest subrepresentation W of (Inj_{K/Z1} F(λ))[m_{K1}²] with [W : τ] = δ_{F(λ),τ} for τ ∈ W_{−ε}; W^{K1} = D_{λ,ε}, W is an extension of ⊕D_{λ+ε_iα_i,ε} by D_{λ,ε}, it is multiplicity-free, with the cosocle and submodule structure of (iv)–(v).
items.note: Statement from v7 read by cc-442dc5; notation as in the paper's §2 and the section named in the locator.

items.name: Corollary 6.3.13 — the representations V_σ
items.statement: For tame ρ̄ with ρ̄|I ≅ τ(s, μ), μ − η 8-deep: (i) the largest V ⊆ (Inj_{K/Z1} τ)[m_{K1}²] with socle τ = ⊕σ^{⊕m_σ} and [V : σ] = m_σ is ⊕V_σ^{⊕m_σ}; (ii) V_σ is multiplicity-free with V_σ^{K1} ≅ D_{λ,ε} and the constituents σ_a with Σ⌊a_i/2⌋ ≤ 1; (iii) JH(V_σ) ∩ JH(V_σ′) = ∅ for σ ≠ σ′.
items.note: Statement from v7 read by cc-442dc5; notation as in the paper's §2 and the section named in the locator.

items.name: Corollary 6.3.15 — V[m_{K1}] is a sum of D_{0,σ}(ρ̄)
items.statement: V[m_{K1}] = ⊕_{σ∈W(ρ̄)} D_{0,σ}(ρ̄)^{⊕m_σ}, with D_{0,σ}(ρ̄) the GL2(k)-representation of [BP12, §13].
items.note: Statement from v7 read by cc-442dc5; notation as in the paper's §2 and the section named in the locator.

items.name: Proposition 6.4.1 — a vanishing on the Iwahori socle
items.statement: For χ = χ_λ with 2 < ⟨λ, α_i^∨⟩ < p − 3 and W of Loewy length 3 with socle and cosocle χ, if Q is a nonzero quotient of Ind_I^K W with [Q : σ_χ] = 1, the composite χ = soc_I(W) ↪ W → Q|_I is zero.
items.note: Statement from v7 read by cc-442dc5; notation as in the paper's §2 and the section named in the locator.

items.name: Lemma 6.4.3 — D_1(ρ̄) is connected
items.statement: For 6-generic ρ̄, D_1(ρ̄) = D_0(ρ̄)^{I1} is connected (Definition 6.4.2), hence so is any semisimple V with JH(V) = JH(D_1(ρ̄)) up to multiplicity.
items.note: Statement from v7 read by cc-442dc5; notation as in the paper's §2 and the section named in the locator.

items.name: Lemma 6.4.4 — Hom from W_{χ,2}
items.statement: For π and D̃ satisfying (a) and (b) and χ = χ_λ ∈ π^{I1} with 2 < ⟨λ, α_i^∨⟩ < p − 3, W_{χ,2} ↠ χ induces Hom_I(χ, π) ≅ Hom_I(W_{χ,2}, π).
items.note: Statement from v7 read by cc-442dc5; notation as in the paper's §2 and the section named in the locator.

items.name: Corollary 6.4.5 — no embedding of E_{χ′,χ}
items.statement: Under Lemma 6.4.4, for χ′ ∈ π^{I1} with Ext¹_{I/Z1}(χ, χ′) ≠ 0 there is no I-equivariant embedding E_{χ′,χ} ↪ π|_I.
items.note: Statement from v7 read by cc-442dc5; notation as in the paper's §2 and the section named in the locator.

items.name: Lemma 7.1.1 — the Bockstein sequence
items.statement: For a K-stable lattice V° with K1 trivial on V°/pV°, the sequence sl_{2,k} ⊗ (V°/pV°) →β V°/pV° →p (V°/p²V°)^{K1} → V°/pV° → 0 is exact.
items.note: Statement from v7 read by cc-442dc5; notation as in the paper's §2 and the section named in the locator.

items.name: Lemma 7.1.2 — β for the adjoint lattice
items.statement: For V° = sl_{2,O_L} ⊗ O, V°/pV° ≅ sl_{2,k} ⊗ F and β(x ⊗ y ⊗ z) = [x, y] ⊗ z.
items.note: Statement from v7 read by cc-442dc5; notation as in the paper's §2 and the section named in the locator.

items.name: Lemma 7.1.4 — Bockstein sequences for sublattices
items.statement: For a K-stable subspace W ⊆ V°/pV° with preimage V_1°, the Bockstein sequences of V_1° and V° form a commutative diagram with exact rows ending in W and V°/pV°.
items.note: Statement from v7 read by cc-442dc5; notation as in the paper's §2 and the section named in the locator.

items.name: Lemma 7.2.1 — ψ_λ is an isomorphism
items.statement: The composite ψ_λ: sl_{2,F} ⊗ L(λ) → sl_{2,F} ⊗ sl_{2,F} ⊗ L(λ) → sl_{2,F} ⊗ L(λ) of Id ⊗ dλ and [−,−] ⊗ Id is an isomorphism of GL2/F-modules.
items.note: Statement from v7 read by cc-442dc5; notation as in the paper's §2 and the section named in the locator.

items.name: Proposition 7.2.2 — Ψ is an isomorphism
items.statement: For λ 2-deep in C_0, the analogous map Ψ: sl_{2,k} ⊗ σ → sl_{2,k} ⊗ σ of GL2(k)-representations is an isomorphism.
items.note: Statement from v7 read by cc-442dc5; notation as in the paper's §2 and the section named in the locator.

items.name: The lattices R_2′ and R
items.statement: R_2 = sl_{2,O_L} ⊗ P̃_σ, R_2′ = {x ∈ R_2 : x mod p ∈ ι(P_σ)}, and R = R_1 ×_{P_σ} R_2′ = {(x_1, x_2) ∈ P̃_σ ⊕ R_2 : x_2 mod p = ι(x_1 mod p)} (57), with r: R → P_σ, (x_1, x_2) ↦ x_1 mod p.
items.note: Statement from v7 read by cc-442dc5; notation as in the paper's §2 and the section named in the locator.

items.name: Proposition 7.3.1 — (R_2′/pR_2′)^{K1} ≅ P_σ
items.statement: Every px (x ∈ R_2) is a sum of (k_i − 1)x_i with k_i ∈ K1, x_i ∈ R_2′, modulo p²R_2; hence (R_2′/pR_2′)^{K1} ↠ P_σ is an isomorphism.
items.note: Statement from v7 read by cc-442dc5; notation as in the paper's §2 and the section named in the locator.

items.name: Lemma 7.3.2 — socle and cosocle of sl_{2,k} ⊗ P_σ
items.statement: σ ↪ P_σ (resp. P_σ ↠ σ) induces sl_{2,k} ⊗ σ ↪ sl_{2,k} ⊗ P_σ (resp. a surjection) whose image is the socle (resp. cosocle).
items.note: Statement from v7 read by cc-442dc5; notation as in the paper's §2 and the section named in the locator.

items.name: Theorem 7.3.3 — the exact sequence for R/pR
items.statement: 0 → R_2/pR_2 → R/pR →r P_σ → 0 is exact, and r induces (R/pR)^{K1} ≅ P_σ.
items.note: Statement from v7 read by cc-442dc5; notation as in the paper's §2 and the section named in the locator.

items.name: Proposition 7.4.1 — commutativity of an endomorphism ring
items.statement: For σ ≅ F(λ) with 2 < ⟨λ, α_i^∨⟩ < p − 4, End_K(Proj_{K/Z1} σ/m_{K1}² Proj_{K/Z1} σ) is commutative.
items.note: Statement from v7 read by cc-442dc5; notation as in the paper's §2 and the section named in the locator.

items.name: Lemma 7.4.2 — cyclicity of Hom
items.statement: Hom_K(R_τ/pR_τ, R/pR) is cyclic as an End_K(R_τ/pR_τ)-module.
items.note: Statement from v7 read by cc-442dc5; notation as in the paper's §2 and the section named in the locator.

items.name: Proposition 7.4.3 — quotients of R/pR are projective relative to subquotients
items.statement: For a quotient Q of R/pR and any subquotient Q′ of Q, R/pR ↠ Q induces Hom_K(Q, Q′) ≅ Hom_K(R/pR, Q′); if cosoc_K(Q′) ≅ σ, there is a K-equivariant surjection Q ↠ Q′.
items.note: Statement from v7 read by cc-442dc5; notation as in the paper's §2 and the section named in the locator.

items.name: Lemma 8.1.2 — cancellation of a power-series variable
items.statement: If R and S are local rings with R[[x]] ≅ S[[x]], then R ≅ S.
items.note: Statement from v7 read by cc-442dc5; notation as in the paper's §2 and the section named in the locator.

items.name: Lemma 8.2.1 — freeness over the support from a submodule and quotient
items.statement: Let N ⊆ M be A-modules and r ≥ 1 with N and M/N free of rank r over their scheme-theoretic supports, M generated by r elements, and Ann(M/N)/Ann(M) ≅ A/Ann(N). Then M is free of rank r over its scheme-theoretic support.
items.note: Statement from v7 read by cc-442dc5; notation as in the paper's §2 and the section named in the locator.

items.name: Lemma 8.2.2 — M∞(σ) is maximal Cohen–Macaulay
items.statement: For any smooth K-representation σ on a finite length W(F)-module, M∞(σ) is maximal CM over its support.
items.note: Statement from v7 read by cc-442dc5; notation as in the paper's §2 and the section named in the locator.

items.name: Proposition 8.2.3 — freeness for Serre weights and tame types
items.statement: There is r ≥ 1 such that (i) M∞(σ_v) is free of rank r over its support, formally smooth over F, for all σ_v ∈ W(r̄_v^∨); (ii) for tame τ with JH(σ(τ)) ∩ W(r̄_v^∨) ≠ ∅ and every K-stable lattice σ°(τ) with irreducible cosocle, M∞(σ°(τ)) is free of rank r over its support, which is a domain.
items.note: Statement from v7 read by cc-442dc5; notation as in the paper's §2 and the section named in the locator.

items.name: Corollary 8.2.4 — lattices in locally algebraic types
items.statement: For σ a sum of nonisomorphic locally algebraic K-representations whose smooth parts are in the image of the inertial local Langlands correspondence and meet W(r̄_v^∨), and σ° a K-stable lattice: M∞(σ°) is maximal CM over its reduced support S, and M∞(σ°) ⊗ E is locally free over S[1/p], which is formally smooth over E.
items.note: Statement from v7 read by cc-442dc5; notation as in the paper's §2 and the section named in the locator.

items.name: Proposition 8.2.6 — freeness of M∞(P̃_{σ_v})
items.statement: For σ_v ∈ W(r̄_v^∨), M∞(P̃_{σ_v}) is free of rank r over R∞/∩_τ p_τ, τ over the tame types with σ_v ∈ JH(σ(τ)) and p_τ = ker(R∞ ↠ R∞^{(1,0),τ}).
items.note: Statement from v7 read by cc-442dc5; notation as in the paper's §2 and the section named in the locator.

items.name: Lemma 8.3.1 — K1-invariance and Loewy length of quotients
items.statement: For a quotient Q of Proj_{K/Z1} σ_v/m_{K1}² with (a) soc_K(Q) in JH(Proj_{K/K1} σ_v) and (b) [Q/soc_K(Q) : σ_v] = 1, rad_K(Q) and Q/S are K1-fixed (S the σ_v-isotypic part of the socle); if moreover (c) soc_K(Q) ⊆ W(r̄_v^∨) and (d) rad_K(Q)/soc_K(Q) meets no weight of W(r̄_v^∨), then Q has Loewy length ≤ 3.
items.note: Statement from v7 read by cc-442dc5; notation as in the paper's §2 and the section named in the locator.

items.name: Lemma 8.3.2 — M∞(R′_{2,j}) is minimally generated by r elements
items.statement: For every j, the R∞-module M∞(R′_{2,j}) is minimally generated by r elements.
items.note: Statement from v7 read by cc-442dc5; notation as in the paper's §2 and the section named in the locator.

items.name: Proposition 8.3.3 — lattices in V(α_j) ⊗ τ°
items.statement: For τ° a GL2(k)-representation on a finite free W(F)-module with τ°[1/p] irreducible and cosocle σ_v, and any K-stable lattice L in (V(α_j) ⊗ τ°)[1/p] with cosocle σ_v, M∞(L) is free of rank r over its support, a domain; such L exists and is unique up to homothety.
items.note: Statement from v7 read by cc-442dc5; notation as in the paper's §2 and the section named in the locator.

items.name: Theorem 8.3.4 — freeness of M∞(R′_{2,j})
items.statement: For j ∈ {0, …, f − 1}, M∞(R′_{2,j}) is free of rank r over R∞/∩_τ p_τ, τ over the tame types with σ_v ∈ JH(σ(τ)) and p_τ = ker(R∞ ↠ R∞^{(2,−1)_j,τ}), where (2,−1)_j is (2,−1) at σ_j and (1,0) elsewhere.
items.note: Statement from v7 read by cc-442dc5; notation as in the paper's §2 and the section named in the locator.

items.name: Lemma 8.3.5 — M∞(T′_{2,j}/pT′_{2,j}) ≅ M∞(Y_j)
items.statement: The surjection T′_{2,j}/pT′_{2,j} ↠ Y_j induces an isomorphism on M∞.
items.note: Statement from v7 read by cc-442dc5; notation as in the paper's §2 and the section named in the locator.

items.name: Lemma 8.3.6 — L_j and N_j agree modulo rad³
items.statement: The surjection R′_{2,j} ↠ T′_{2,j} induces L_j ↠ N_j and an isomorphism (L_j/pL_j)/rad³ ≅ (N_j/pN_j)/rad³.
items.note: L_j = L_{j−1} ×_{P_σv} R′_{2,j} (76), L_{−1} = P̃_{σv}, and N_j = L_{j−1} ×_{Y_j} T′_{2,j}. Statement from v7 read by cc-442dc5; notation as in the paper's §2 and the section named in the locator.

items.name: Proposition 8.3.7 — generation of M∞(L_j) and M∞(N_j)
items.statement: M∞(L_j) is generated by r elements if and only if M∞(N_j) is.
items.note: Statement from v7 read by cc-442dc5; notation as in the paper's §2 and the section named in the locator.

items.name: Lemma 8.3.8 — freeness of fibre products
items.statement: For a commutative noetherian local R and nonzero M_1, M_2, M free of rank r over their supports with surjections M_i ↠ M: Ann(M_1 ×_M M_2) = Ann(M_1) ∩ Ann(M_2), and M_1 ×_M M_2 is free of rank r over its support iff Ann(M) = Ann(M_1) + Ann(M_2) iff Ann(M) ⊆ Ann(M_1) + Ann(M_2).
items.note: Statement from v7 read by cc-442dc5; notation as in the paper's §2 and the section named in the locator.

items.name: Corollary 8.3.10 — freeness of M∞(R)
items.statement: M∞(R) is free of rank r over R∞/∩_{λ,τ} p_{λ,τ} (λ_j ∈ {(1,0),(2,−1)} for all j); in particular dim_F M∞(R)/m∞ = r.
items.note: Statement from v7 read by cc-442dc5; notation as in the paper's §2 and the section named in the locator.

items.name: Theorem 8.3.11 — M∞ of the projective quotient
items.statement: (Proj_{K/Z1} σ_v)/m_{K1}² ↠ σ_v induces an isomorphism M∞((Proj σ_v)/m_{K1}²)/m∞ ≅ M∞(σ_v)/m∞ of nonzero finite-dimensional F-vector spaces.
items.note: Statement from v7 read by cc-442dc5; notation as in the paper's §2 and the section named in the locator.

items.name: Theorem 8.4.3 — M∞ is faithfully flat
items.statement: The R∞-module M∞ is faithfully flat.
items.note: Statement from v7 read by cc-442dc5; notation as in the paper's §2 and the section named in the locator.
